f3_program: observe(at("james.main_job.earnings.rate", "current"), 20, "dollar_per_hour", source("James earns $20 an hour while working at his main job"))
percent_less(at("james.second_job.earnings.rate", "current"), at("james.main_job.earnings.rate", "current"), 20, source("He earns 20% less while working his second job"))
observe(at("james.main_job.work.duration", "per_week"), 30, "hour", source("He works 30 hours at his main job"))
fraction_of(at("james.second_job.work.duration", "per_week"), at("james.main_job.work.duration", "per_week"), 1, 2, source("half that much at his second job"))
assumptions: The second-job percentage is resolved against James's preceding hourly earnings rate, and the work durations are interpreted within the weekly period named by the query.
Answering requires unstated quarter-to-nickel denomination conversion knowledge and the unstated standard value of an ordinary nickel, which F3-v1 does not allow annotators to invent.

f3_program: observe(at("jackson.spending_money.earning_rate", "current"), 5, "dollar_per_hour", source("She promises $5 per hour spent on chores"))
multiple(at("jackson.chores.bathroom_cleaning.duration", "current"), at("jackson.chores.dishwashing.duration", "current"), 3, source("three times as long cleaning the bathroom"))
assumptions: “this” is resolved to the immediately preceding vacuuming activity, and “three times as long” is resolved against the immediately preceding dishwashing duration.

f3_program: observe(at("jenna.business.rent.expense", "month"), 10000, "dollar", source("Every month she has to pay $10,000 in rent"))
percent_of(at("jenna.business.tax.expense", "month"), at("jenna.business.tax.profit_base", "month"), 20, source("20% of her total profit in taxes"))
assumptions: The source does not specify whether “total profit” serving as the tax base means pre-tax profit or the final profit queried; equating either interpretation would materially change the result.

f3_program: offset(at("julia.baking.cake_rate", "current"), at("julia.baking.reference_rate", "current"), -1, "cake_per_day", source("one less than 5 cakes per day"))
rate_relation("julia.baking.total_cakes_produced", at("julia.baking.cake_rate", "current"), at("julia.baking.duration", "current"), source("bakes one less than 5 cakes per day for 6 days"))
produce("julia_baking", "julia", at("julia.cakes.count", "current"), "julia.baking.total_cakes_produced", source("Julia bakes one less than 5 cakes per day for 6 days"))
observe(at("clifford.cake_eating.cakes_per_active_day", "current"), 1, "cake_per_day", source("every other day, Julia's brother, Clifford, sneaks into Julia's house and eats one of Julia's cakes"))

rate_relation("clifford.cake_eating.total_cakes_consumed", at("clifford.cake_eating.cakes_per_active_day", "current"), at("clifford.cake_eating.active_duration", "current"), source("every other day, Julia's brother, Clifford, sneaks into Julia's house and eats one of Julia's cakes"))

consume("clifford_eating", "clifford", at("julia.cakes.count", "current"), "clifford.cake_eating.total_cakes_consumed", source("every other day, Julia's brother, Clifford, sneaks into Julia's house and eats one of Julia's cakes"))
assumptions: Across the stated six-day interval, “every other day” is represented as one-half of the interval, with one cake consumed on each active day.
